question: Pandit Ram Narayan is a Hindustani Classical musician who plays ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarangi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ram Narayan (1927–2017) was a legendary Hindustani classical musician, renowned for elevating the sarangi (सारंगी — तार वाला भारतीय शास्त्रीय वाद्य) from a mere accompanying instrument to a solo concert instrument.

 

• He was the first sarangi player to establish it as an independent solo concert instrument on the international stage and was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 2005.

 

• He received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1975 and is often referred to as the "Sarangi Ustad" for his mastery over the instrument.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument, traditionally used to accompany vocal music and Kathak dance performances.

 

• Other renowned sarangi players include Ustad Sultan Khan and Ustad Bundu Khan.

 

NOTE

 

• Flute (Option 1): Associated with maestros like Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, not Pandit Ram Narayan.

 

• Harmonium (Option 2): A keyboard reed instrument used mainly for vocal accompaniment; not Ram Narayan's instrument.

 

• Tabla (Option 4): A pair of hand drums; renowned players include Ustad Zakir Hussain and Ustad Alla Rakha, not Pandit Ram Narayan.

question: In which year was Battle of Peshawar fought between Raja Jayapal and Mahmud Ghazni?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1001.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Peshawar was fought in 1001 CE between Raja Jayapala, the Hindu Shahi ruler of Gandhara/Punjab, and Mahmud of Ghazni (महमूद ग़ज़नवी).

 

• Jayapala was defeated and later abdicated the throne in favour of his son Anandapala, out of shame at his defeat.

 

• This was the first of Mahmud Ghazni's seventeen invasions of India, marking the beginning of repeated raids into the Indian subcontinent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jayapala's son Anandapala later fought Mahmud again at the Battle of Chach (Waihind) around 1008–1009 CE, also losing.

 

• Mahmud Ghazni is infamous for repeatedly raiding and plundering Indian temples, most notably the Somnath temple in 1025 CE.

 

NOTE

 

• 1112 (Option 2): Mahmud Ghazni had already died in 1030 CE; no such battle occurred in 1112.

 

• 1305 (Option 3): This period falls under the Delhi Sultanate (Alauddin Khalji's reign), unrelated to Jayapala or Mahmud Ghazni.

 

• 1258 (Option 4): This year is associated with the Mongol sack of Baghdad, unrelated to the Battle of Peshawar.

question: Union Home Minister Amit Shah unveiled 14 feet high statue of Lok Nayak Jayprakash Narayan in ______ in October 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 11 October 2022 (the birth anniversary of Jayaprakash Narayan), Union Home Minister Amit Shah unveiled a 14-feet-high statue of Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan at Sitab Diara, JP's birthplace in Saran district, Bihar, and also addressed a public meeting there.

 

• Jayaprakash Narayan (1902–1979), popularly called "Lok Nayak" (लोकनायक — जन नायक), led the Sampoorna Kranti (Total Revolution) movement of the 1970s against the Emergency.

 

• Sitab Diara is a village situated on the border of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the Ganga and Saryu rivers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• JP Narayan was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

 

• The Sampoorna Kranti movement is considered a major precursor to the imposition of the National Emergency (1975–1977) by Indira Gandhi's government.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand, West Bengal, Maharashtra (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these states is connected to this event; both JP Narayan's birthplace and the 2022 statue unveiling are located in Bihar.

question: Dhupgarh peak is the highest point of which of the following States of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dhupgarh, located near Pachmarhi in the Satpura Range, is the highest point of Madhya Pradesh at an elevation of about 1,352 metres (4,429 ft).

 

• It lies within the Satpura National Park / Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve in the Narmadapuram (Hoshangabad) district of Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Dhupgarh is well known for its scenic sunrise and sunset views and is a popular trekking destination.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pachmarhi is the only hill station in Madhya Pradesh and is often called the "Satpura ki Rani" (Queen of Satpura, सतपुड़ा की रानी).

 

• The Satpura Range runs roughly parallel to the Vindhya Range, with the Narmada River flowing in the valley between them.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh (Options 1, 2, 3): Dhupgarh does not lie within any of these states — it is located entirely within Madhya Pradesh, so none of them can claim it as their highest point.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct?
I. Death rate in India is 7.2 per 1000 in 2011.
II. Life expectancy at birth is 72.6 years in 2012.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Sample Registration System (SRS) data, India's Crude Death Rate (CDR) was around 7.1–7.2 per 1000 population in 2011, so Statement I is correct.

 

• However, India's actual average life expectancy at birth around 2012 was approximately 66–68 years, not 72.6 years — so Statement II is incorrect; the figure of 72.6 years does not match India's official data for that period.

 

• Since only Statement I holds true, the correct choice is "Only I."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's life expectancy has since risen; SRS 2015–19 data placed it at around 69.7 years.

 

• The Crude Death Rate has continued its long-term decline due to improved healthcare, sanitation, and nutrition.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): Incorrect, as Statement II's life expectancy figure is inflated and does not match India's actual 2012 data.

 

• Both I and II (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement II is false.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement I is actually true.

question: In which month, Hiroshima Day is observed across the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is August.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hiroshima Day is observed on 6 August every year to commemorate the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, Japan, by the United States on 6 August 1945, during World War II.

 

• A second atomic bomb was dropped on Nagasaki three days later, on 9 August 1945.

 

• The day is observed worldwide to promote nuclear disarmament and world peace.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The bomb dropped on Hiroshima was code-named "Little Boy"; the one on Nagasaki was code-named "Fat Man."

 

• Japan formally surrendered on 15 August 1945, marking the end of World War II.

 

NOTE

 

• October, January, July (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these months corresponds to the actual date of the Hiroshima bombing, which occurred on 6 August 1945.

question: The monetary policy instrument called ‘bank rate’ is aligned to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marginal standing facility rate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bank Rate is the rate at which the RBI lends long-term funds to commercial banks, under Section 49 of the RBI Act, 1934.

 

• Since May 2011, the RBI has kept the Bank Rate aligned with the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate — both move automatically and simultaneously whenever the MSF rate is revised.

 

• The MSF rate itself is generally maintained at 25 basis points above the repo rate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bank Rate is used for penalising banks that fail to meet CRR/SLR requirements and for computing penal interest.

 

• The Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) comprises repo and reverse repo operations used for day-to-day liquidity management, distinct from the Bank Rate.

 

NOTE

 

• Liquidity adjustment facility (Option 1): A mechanism using repo/reverse repo rates for short-term liquidity management, separate from the Bank Rate mechanism.

 

• Cash Reserve Ratio (Option 2): The percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be kept with the RBI; not linked to the Bank Rate.

 

• Discount rate (Option 3): A general term for the interest rate charged on advances; not the officially notified RBI instrument aligned to the Bank Rate.

question: ISRO successfully launched the communication satellite GSAT-24 from _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kourou in French Guiana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• GSAT-24, a 24 Ku-band transponder communication satellite of ISRO, was launched on 23 June 2022 aboard an Ariane-5 rocket from the Kourou Spaceport in French Guiana.

 

• It was the first satellite mission of NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), fully funded and leased for DTH services (leased to Tata Play).

 

• The launch was carried out through Arianespace, the French commercial launch service provider.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kourou spaceport is operated in cooperation with the European Space Agency (ESA), CNES, and Arianespace.

 

• ISRO's own satellite launches from Sriharikota (India) typically use the PSLV and GSLV launch vehicles; GSAT-24 required the heavier-lift Ariane-5 due to its mass.

 

NOTE

 

• Moscow in Russia, Chicago in US, Berlin in Germany (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these cities hosts the orbital launch facility used for this mission; GSAT-24 was actually launched from Kourou, French Guiana.

question:
Which of the following is correct regarding the respiration?
I. Regular traditional breathing exercise (pranayama) can increase the capacity of lungs to take in more air.
II. During inhalation, ribs move up and outwards and diaphragm moves down.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: Regular practice of pranayama (breathing exercises) increases lung capacity by strengthening the respiratory muscles and improving alveolar ventilation.

 

• Statement II is correct: During inhalation, the intercostal muscles contract, causing the ribs to move upward and outward, while the diaphragm contracts and flattens, moving downward — both actions increase the volume of the thoracic cavity, lowering internal pressure and drawing air into the lungs.

 

• Since both statements accurately describe respiratory physiology, "Both I and II" is the correct choice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• During exhalation, the reverse occurs: the ribs move down and inward, and the diaphragm relaxes and moves upward.

 

• Pranayama techniques such as Anulom-Vilom and Kapalbhati are widely practised to improve respiratory efficiency and lung capacity.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because Statement I is also true.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 3): Incorrect, because both statements are actually true.

 

• Only I (Option 4): Incorrect, because Statement II is also true.

question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to make the contents of a cell italic in MS-Excel 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl + 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS Excel (including Excel 365), Ctrl + 3 is the keyboard shortcut used to toggle italic formatting for the selected cell content (equivalent to Ctrl + I).

 

• Related number-based shortcuts: Ctrl + 2 applies/removes Bold, Ctrl + 4 applies/removes Underline, and Ctrl + 5 applies/removes Strikethrough.

 

• These shortcuts work alongside the more commonly known letter-based shortcuts (Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ctrl + 1 opens the "Format Cells" dialog box in Excel, giving access to all formatting options.

 

• These number-key formatting shortcuts are largely consistent across most Microsoft Office applications.

 

NOTE

 

• Ctrl + 4 (Option 1): Toggles underline formatting, not italic.

 

• Ctrl + 6 (Option 3): Used to toggle the display of objects in certain versions of Excel, not italic formatting.

 

• Ctrl + 2 (Option 4): Toggles bold formatting, not italic.

question: What are hardware devices that retrieves data from a computer system and further translates the received data into a form understandable to humans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Output Devices.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Output devices are hardware components that retrieve/receive data from a computer system (after processing) and convert or translate it into a human-understandable form, such as text, images, or sound.

 

• Common examples include monitors, printers, speakers, and projectors.

 

• They constitute the final stage of the input–process–output cycle of a computer system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Soft-copy output devices include the monitor and speaker; hard-copy output devices include the printer and plotter.

 

• Some devices, such as touchscreens, function as both input and output devices simultaneously.

 

NOTE

 

• Processor (Option 1): The CPU, which processes data internally; it does not itself convert data into a human-readable form for presentation.

 

• Input Devices (Option 2): Devices like the keyboard and mouse that feed data into the computer — the opposite function of output devices.

 

• Storage Devices (Option 3): Devices like hard disks and pen drives that store data, rather than display or present it to users.

question: Who of the following person wrote a book named Kitab-ul-Hind?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Al-Biruni.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kitab-ul-Hind (also called Tahqiq-i-Hind) was written by Al-Biruni (अलबरूनी), an 11th-century Persian polymath and scholar who accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni to India.

 

• The book is a detailed account of Indian society, religion, philosophy, and science, written in Arabic around 1030 CE.

 

• Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit to study Indian texts directly, making his account one of the most authentic contemporary sources on early medieval India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Al-Biruni is also credited with early scientific estimations, including a calculation of the Earth's radius, and contributions to mathematics and astronomy.

 

• Other notable foreign chroniclers of India include Ibn Battuta (Rehla) and Megasthenes (Indica).

 

NOTE

 

• Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma (Option 1): A pre-Islamic Arabian poet, one of the authors of the Mu'allaqat; unrelated to India.

 

• Antara Ibn Shaddad (Option 2): A pre-Islamic Arab warrior-poet, also one of the Mu'allaqat poets, unrelated to India.

 

• Imru' al-Qais (Option 4): Often considered the father of Arabic poetry and another Mu'allaqat poet; none of these three wrote about India.

question: ______ percent can be taken as the average value for the amount of organic matter that is present at each step of food chain and reaches the next level of consumers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ten Percent Law (Lindeman's Law of trophic efficiency) states that only about 10% of the energy/organic matter available at one trophic level is transferred to the next level in a food chain; the rest is lost as heat, through respiration, and as unconsumed matter.

 

• This principle explains why food chains typically consist of only 4–5 trophic levels, since the energy remaining becomes insufficient to support further levels.

 

• The law was proposed by ecologist Raymond Lindeman in 1942.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This law underlies the shape of the ecological pyramid of energy, which is always upright, unlike pyramids of biomass or numbers.

 

• It also explains why the biomass of top carnivores is always much smaller than that of producers in an ecosystem.

 

NOTE

 

• 5, 20, 2 (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these matches the standard ecological approximation used for energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels, which is 10%.

question: Which amendment in the Indian constitution is related to extension of jurisdiction of High Courts to Union territories?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7th Amendment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, reorganised states on a linguistic basis and amended Article 230 to extend the jurisdiction of High Courts to Union Territories.

 

• It also enabled the establishment of common High Courts for two or more states.

 

• This amendment was passed alongside the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 214 provides that there shall be a High Court for each state, while Article 231 allows for common High Courts for two or more states.

 

• India currently has 25 High Courts, several of which have jurisdiction extending over more than one state or Union Territory.

 

NOTE

 

• 9th Amendment (Option 1): Related to the transfer of certain Indian territories to Pakistan following a border settlement (1960).

 

• 1st Amendment (Option 3): Added the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution and placed reasonable restrictions on the freedom of speech (1951).

 

• 13th Amendment (Option 4): Created Nagaland as the 16th state of India (1962).

question: Which of the following sports was NOT played at Tokyo Olympics 2020 held in 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mallakhamba.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Table Tennis, Fencing, and Volleyball are all internationally recognised Olympic sports and were part of the official Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021) program.

 

• Mallakhamba (मल्लखंब) is a traditional Indian sport involving gymnastic exercises performed on a vertical wooden pole or hanging rope; it is not an Olympic sport.

 

• Since Mallakhamba was not contested at the Tokyo Olympics, it is the correct answer to this question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Efforts continue to promote Mallakhamba internationally, including attempts to secure recognition from global sports federations.

 

• Tokyo 2020 introduced new sports to the Olympic program for the first time, including Karate, Skateboarding, Sport Climbing, and Surfing.

 

NOTE

 

• Table Tennis (Option 1), Fencing (Option 2), Volleyball (Option 4): All are established Olympic sports and were contested at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games.

question: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance of ____________ in southern India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in the temples of Tamil Nadu (तमिलनाडु), particularly associated with the Thanjavur region.

 

• It traditionally follows the principles laid out in the Natya Shastra, attributed to sage Bharata Muni.

 

• The dance form was historically performed by Devadasis in temples and was revived and popularised in its modern form during the 20th century by figures like Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The "Thanjavur Quartet" (four brothers — Chinnayya, Ponnayya, Sivanandam, and Vadivelu) are credited with systematising Bharatanatyam into its present form.

 

• Bharatanatyam is characterised by a fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate footwork, and an elaborate vocabulary of hand gestures (mudras).

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Known for classical dance forms such as Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Known for the Yakshagana dance-drama form.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Known for the classical dance form Kuchipudi.

question: सोवा वायरस (SOVA Virus) जिसे हाल ही में ख़बरों में देखा गया है, एक ______ है।
option_4: मवेशी में पाया जाने वाला वायरस
solution_text:
The correct answer is मालवेयर (Malware).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• SOVA एक Android बैंकिंग ट्रोजन (मालवेयर) है जो Chrome, Amazon जैसे वैध ऐप्स का रूप धारण कर बैंकिंग क्रेडेंशियल चुराता है, keystrokes रिकॉर्ड करता है, और OTP इंटरसेप्ट करता है। (SOVA is an Android banking Trojan malware that disguises itself as legitimate apps.)

 

• इसे पहली बार 2021 के मध्य में देखा गया था, और 2022 तक इसके नए वर्ज़न में रैनसमवेयर जैसी क्षमताएं भी जुड़ गईं, जो संक्रमित डिवाइस की फाइलों को एन्क्रिप्ट कर सकती थीं।

 

• साइबर सुरक्षा शोधकर्ताओं (जैसे Cleafy) ने SOVA को भारत सहित कई देशों में बैंकिंग ऐप्स को निशाना बनाने वाले एक बढ़ते खतरे के रूप में चिन्हित किया।

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• SOVA मुख्यतः Google Play Store के बाहर के नकली/दुर्भावनापूर्ण ऐप्स और फ़िशिंग लिंक के माध्यम से फैलता है।

 

• उपयोगकर्ताओं को केवल विश्वसनीय स्रोतों से ही ऐप्स इंस्टॉल करने और Play Protect सक्षम रखने की सलाह दी जाती है।

 

NOTE

 

• कोविड-19 का प्रकार (Option 2): SOVA कोविड-19 का कोई प्रकार (variant) नहीं है; यह एक डिजिटल मालवेयर खतरा है, जैविक वायरस से असंबंधित।

 

• मंकी वायरस का प्रकार (Option 3): SOVA का Monkeypox वायरस से कोई संबंध नहीं है।

 

• मवेशी में पाया जाने वाला वायरस (Option 4): SOVA पशुओं का वायरस नहीं है (जैसे Lumpy Skin Disease वायरस); यह एक कंप्यूटर मालवेयर है।

question: What is the official language of Bhutan, a neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dzongkha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dzongkha (द्ज़ोंग्खा) is the official and national language of Bhutan, written in the Tibetan (Ucchen) script.

 

• It is spoken primarily in western Bhutan and is the medium of instruction, alongside English, in Bhutanese schools.

 

• Bhutan's official currency is the Ngultrum, and its capital is Thimphu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhutan is officially known as the "Kingdom of Bhutan" and is well known for measuring national progress through Gross National Happiness (GNH) rather than GDP alone.

 

• Bhutan shares its borders with India (to the south, east, and west) and China/Tibet (to the north).

 

NOTE

 

• Yuan (Option 1): The currency of China, not a language.

 

• Ngultrum (Option 3): The official currency of Bhutan, not its language.

 

• Kyat (Option 4): The currency of Myanmar, unrelated to Bhutan.

question: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Act made the Right to education a Fundamental Right under article 21 A of the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (Eighty-Sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.

 

• This amendment also added Article 51A(k), making it a fundamental duty of parents/guardians to provide educational opportunities to their children.

 

• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, was subsequently enacted to give effect to Article 21A, coming into force on 1 April 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21A falls under Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution, distinguishing it from the earlier non-justiciable Directive Principle under Article 45.

 

• Prior to this amendment, education for children was addressed only as a Directive Principle of State Policy, which was not enforceable in courts.

 

NOTE

 

• 91st Amendment Act, 2003 (Option 1): Related to limiting the size of the Council of Ministers and strengthening anti-defection provisions.

 

• 89th Amendment Act, 2003 (Option 3): Related to the bifurcation of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into two separate commissions.

 

• 19th Amendment Act, 1966 (Option 4): Related to the abolition of Election Tribunals, transferring election dispute jurisdiction to High Courts.

question: Which country will host the 2024 Summer Olympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is France.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• France (specifically the city of Paris) hosted the 2024 Summer Olympic Games, officially known as the Games of the XXXIII Olympiad.

 

• Paris had previously hosted the Olympics in 1900 and 1924, making 2024 its third time hosting — placing it among the few cities (alongside London) to host the Summer Games three times.

 

• The 2024 Paralympics were also held in Paris, immediately following the Olympics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2020 Summer Olympics were hosted by Tokyo, Japan (actually held in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic).

 

• The 2028 Summer Olympics are scheduled to be hosted by Los Angeles, USA.

 

NOTE

 

• Germany, Switzerland, England (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these countries was selected to host the 2024 Summer Olympics; the host was France (Paris).

question: Which state hosted the 36th National Games in the year 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 36th National Games of India were hosted by Gujarat in 2022, with events held across multiple cities, including Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara, and Rajkot.

 

• The Games were inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 29 September 2022 and concluded on 12 October 2022.

 

• This was the first time Gujarat hosted the National Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Services (SSCB) topped the medal tally at the 36th National Games, with Maharashtra and Haryana also among the top-performing contingents.

 

• The subsequent 37th National Games were held in Goa in 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh, Goa, Maharashtra (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these states hosted the 36th National Games in 2022; the actual host was Gujarat.

question: The first woman to win the Dronacharya Award was weightlifting coach ______ in 2000.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hansa Sharma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hansa Sharma became the first woman to receive the Dronacharya Award, conferred in 2000, for her contribution to coaching weightlifting.

 

• The Dronacharya Award, instituted in 1985 by the Government of India, honours outstanding sports coaches for producing internationally successful, medal-winning athletes.

 

• Her recognition marked a significant milestone for women coaches in Indian sports, a field that had traditionally been male-dominated.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Purnima Mahato, an archery coach, later won the Dronacharya Award in 2009 for coaching Indian archers such as Deepika Kumari.

 

• The Dronacharya Award is presented annually by the President of India, alongside other National Sports Awards such as the Khel Ratna and Arjuna Award.

 

NOTE

 

• Sunita Sharma (Option 1): Not recorded as the first woman Dronacharya awardee.

 

• Renu Kohli (Option 2): A basketball coach who received the Dronacharya Award at a later date, but not as the first woman recipient in 2000 for weightlifting.

 

• Purnima Mahato (Option 3): An accomplished archery coach who won the Dronacharya Award years later, in 2009, not in 2000.

question: When lead nitrate is heated, then which of the following gases is produced?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitrogen dioxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When lead nitrate [Pb(NO₃)₂] is heated, it undergoes thermal decomposition to give lead oxide (PbO), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂, reddish-brown fumes), and oxygen gas (O₂).

 

• The reaction: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂↑ + O₂↑.

 

• This is a classic thermal decomposition reaction demonstrated in school chemistry, easily identified by the characteristic brown fumes and crackling sound.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This decomposition reaction is used in the NCERT chemistry curriculum to illustrate the thermal decomposition of nitrate salts.

 

• Most heavy-metal nitrates decompose on heating to give the metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen — unlike alkali metal nitrates, which typically decompose to give the metal nitrite and oxygen only.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrogen oxide (Option 1): Not the correct/primary gas produced; the characteristic brown gas released is specifically nitrogen dioxide (NO₂).

 

• Lead dioxide (Option 2): Not a gas, and not a product of this decomposition; the solid product formed is lead monoxide (PbO).

 

• Lead oxide (Option 4): This is indeed a product of the reaction, but it is a solid residue, not a gas — the question specifically asks about the gas produced.

question:
The simultaneous shifts of both the demand curve and the supply curve can happen in which of the following ways?
I. Supply curve shifts leftward and demand curve shifts rightward.
II. Both supply and demand curves shift leftwards.
III. Supply curve shifts rightward and demand curve shifts leftward.
solution_text:
The correct answer is I, II and III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When both the demand curve and the supply curve shift simultaneously, several combinations of movement are possible, since each curve can independently shift left, right, or remain unchanged.

 

• Statement I (supply shifts left, demand shifts right) is a valid combination — for example, occurring when input costs rise while consumer income also rises.

 

• Statement II (both curves shift left) and Statement III (supply shifts right, demand shifts left) are also valid, realistic combinations that occur under different economic conditions (e.g., a supply shock alongside falling consumer preference, or improved production technology alongside a demand-reducing shock).

 

• Since all three combinations — I, II, and III — represent genuinely possible ways in which simultaneous shifts of both curves can occur, all are correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• When both curves shift in the same direction, the effect on equilibrium price is ambiguous (depends on the relative magnitude of the shifts), while the effect on quantity is unambiguous (both increase, or both decrease).

 

• When the curves shift in opposite directions, the effect on equilibrium quantity is ambiguous, while the effect on price is unambiguous.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, since Statements II and III also describe valid simultaneous-shift scenarios.

 

• II and III (Option 2): Incomplete, since Statement I is also a valid scenario.

 

• I and II (Option 3): Incomplete, since Statement III is also a valid scenario.

question: The Earth has been divided into many time zones. How many degrees does each time zone covers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15 degrees.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Earth completes one full 360° rotation on its axis in 24 hours, so it rotates 360° ÷ 24 = 15° per hour.

 

• Consequently, the Earth is divided into 24 standard time zones, each spanning 15 degrees of longitude, representing a difference of one hour in local time.

 

• Moving 15° eastward advances local time by one hour, while moving 15° westward sets it back by one hour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India follows a single time zone, Indian Standard Time (IST), based on 82.5° E longitude (passing near Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh), which is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT.

 

• The Prime Meridian (0°) passes through Greenwich, England, and serves as the reference line for calculating time zones worldwide.

 

NOTE

 

• 24 degrees, 20 degrees, 10 degrees (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these correctly represents the standard division used for each of the 24 time zones (360° ÷ 24 = 15°).
